title: Stripe Connect Alternatives: Which One Fits Your Platform?
description: A decision guide for non-US marketplace operators and commission platforms. Answer three questions to find the Stripe Connect alternative path that fits your sellers, partners, and geography.
text: Decision guide · Non-US platforms Stripe Connect Alternatives: Which One Fits Your Platform? Don't read every platform profile. Answer three questions. Go straight to the section that fits your platform. Find the right section 1. Who mainly gets the money after it comes in? Sellers or service providers Partners or channel affiliates Only my own business Not sure you want to be the seller of record at all? Skip to the Merchant of Record route You do not need a Connect replacement if you have no split-payment requirement. Go to the Stripe Alternatives Hub 2. Before paying sellers, do you need to hold the funds? Yes (holding / escrow required) No (direct split / payout) 3. Where are your sellers mainly located? Europe Outside Europe, mostly one region Outside Europe, across continents Show my section View all 6 paths C1-C6 = Stripe Connect & Marketplace Routing Paths Quick reference: all six paths Your profile Path Shortlist Seller payouts, no holding, one region C1 PayPal Commerce; Dodo (MoR, digital only) Seller payouts, no holding, cross-continent C2 Airwallex, Nuvei, PayPal Commerce; PayU if sellers concentrate in EE/LatAm/India/Africa Seller payouts, holding required, Europe C3 Mangopay, OPP, Ryft, Lemonway Seller payouts, holding required, outside Europe C4 Airwallex, Checkout.com, Rapyd Partner revenue share, simple rules C5 PayPal, Airwallex, Tipalti Partner revenue share, complex rules C6 Adyen, Braintree; Worldpay (enterprise); Finix (US/Canada only) The interactive checklist needs JavaScript. Enable JavaScript, or use the section headings in the article below to jump to the path that matches your situation. Built for non-US marketplaces and commission platforms splitting payments among businesses — no US entity required. What this is: A routing shortlist, not an approval guarantee. You still need to verify country coverage, legal models, underwriting, and contract terms. Before you start: If price is your only issue, check when to stay on Stripe Connect first — it often remains the best fit for simple setups. Path C1 Path C1: Seller payouts, no fund holding, mostly one region One honest check first: this profile — simple splits, one region, no holding — is also the profile where staying on Stripe Connect often wins. If nothing is actually broken beyond rates, read when to stay on Connect before shortlisting anyone. Shortlist PayPal Commerce — a simple regional payout flow needs recipient familiarity and a workable selling model, not a complex wallet. If the flow later grows into multi-party splitting, Braintree (PayPal Enterprise Payments) is the same-ecosystem upgrade — but a single-region, no-holding payout does not need it today. Dodo (MoR) — if you don't want to touch the money at all. The provider becomes the seller of record, not your platform, and MoR underwriting generally covers digital products and SaaS only, not physical goods or in-person services. 1 Compare the model on the Merchant of Record Hub before shortlisting. Skip / Watch-outs Skip Mangopay and OPP for now. A wallet-centered model is unnecessary if you do not hold funds. Skip Adyen. A broader platform integration is more than a single-region payout flow needs. If holding may become a requirement later — disputes, staged releases, refund windows — read Path C3 before discarding the wallet providers. Don't confuse "can pay a creator" with "supports your marketplace." Confirm who is seller of record. Confirm who handles disputes. Confirm what onboarding recipients need. Confirm whether the route works from your country. PayPal's payout features vary by country. 2 Next steps Your next due-diligence checks: Check PayPal Commerce payout availability by country Check whether Dodo's Merchant of Record model fits your product Shortlisted PayPal Commerce? Model their real all-in cost — processing, FX, payouts, and hidden fees — against your monthly GTV and cross-border share. Open the payment cost calculator Path C2 Path C2: Seller payouts, no holding, cross-continent Shortlist Nuvei — strongest fit when sellers span multiple continents and need local methods beyond cards: 720+ payment methods, 150+ currencies, 50+ local acquiring markets. 18 Pending acquisition of Payoneer (announced June 2026, expected mid-2027) will fold mass-payout and multi-currency accounts into the same entity. 22 Until that closes, treat Payoneer as a standalone option with a known integration horizon — confirm transition terms before building a long-term stack around it. Airwallex — strong cross-border multi-currency infrastructure. Caveat: features depend on your incorporation country and on the licenses of the Airwallex entity serving that market — the same API exposes different modules under different entities. Confirm availability first. 3 4 PayPal Commerce — lightweight starting point for pure cross-border disbursement. If the flow later needs marketplace-grade splitting, upgrade within the same ecosystem to Braintree (PayPal Enterprise Payments) . 20 Rapyd — another full-stack candidate with broad local-method and payout corridor coverage. PayU Split Settlements — if sellers concentrate in Eastern Europe (Poland, Romania, Turkey), Latin America (Colombia, Brazil), India, or Africa, PayU is the regionally dominant option. It splits a single customer payment among multiple sellers with commission, discount, and tax handling in the same transaction. 23 Confirm seller-country coverage and settlement currency first; its strength is corridor depth, not global breadth. Local champions — if recipients concentrate in one region outside Europe, also check dLocal or EBANX (Latin America), Xendit (Southeast Asia), Razorpay (India), Flutterwave (Africa). The same country-by-country matrix applies: entity, onboarding, currencies, payout routes. Payout-only layers — pair with your acquiring setup rather than replacing it: Hyperwallet (PayPal's mass-payout arm) or Trolley (mass payouts with built-in tax-form collection) for recipient operations and tax forms; Wise Platform or Thunes for underlying disbursement rails. Thunes sits closer to the network and usually works under a disbursement layer, not as a replacement for Hyperwallet or Trolley. Skip / Watch-outs Skip Mangopay. A wallet-based flow is unnecessary when you do not hold funds. Skip Finix. Confirm fit for your operating countries and entity structure first. Two execution traps: "International payouts" is not one feature — build a country-by-country matrix covering legal entity, buyer and seller locations, settlement currencies, onboarding, and payout methods; a provider may cover part of the chain without the whole chain. 2 And treat recipient onboarding as a conversion funnel, not a checkbox — a foreign KYC/KYB flow or a forced new wallet costs you sellers at signup, often more than the headline payout fee. Next steps Your next due-diligence checks: Compare Airwallex platform payout routes and country coverage Check PayPal recipient payout support by country Compare Rapyd's local-method and payout corridor coverage Review Nuvei's cross-border payout and local-method coverage Review PayU Split Settlements for multi-seller marketplaces Shortlisted Airwallex, Nuvei, PayPal, or Rapyd? Model their real all-in cost — processing, FX, payouts, and hidden fees — against your monthly GTV and cross-border share. Open the payment cost calculator Path C3 Path C3: Seller payouts, holding required, Europe Shortlist Mangopay — documents an electronic-wallet model; wallets hold funds processed on behalf of platforms and users. 5 OPP , Ryft , and Lemonway — Lemonway is a France-licensed provider specializing in regulated safeguarding of marketplace funds. Treat all four as candidates for a legal and operational review, not an automatic escrow shortlist. The question is not whether money can remain unpaid for a while — it is who legally holds it, under what arrangement, and what event releases it. Skip / Watch-outs Do not shortlist a delayed-payout feature as escrow. Timing alone does not create escrow's legal protections. Do not select a provider from a Europe label alone. Supported countries matter. The platform's entity matters. Recipient onboarding matters. The custody arrangement matters. Stripe says manual payouts hold funds in a connected account balance — and that it does not provide escrow services. 6 "Escrow" on the product page is not proof. Ask five questions. Which entity holds the money? Are funds segregated? What are the release conditions? What is the dispute and refund process? In which countries is the arrangement permitted? If the answer is only "we can delay payouts," you have not confirmed escrow. Mollie Connect is worth a look for standard European e-commerce splitting — clean integration and strong local methods like iDEAL and Bancontact. 24 But its custody and complex-disbursement tooling is lighter than wallet-native providers like Mangopay or Lemonway, so for a holding-required flow it is not the route. Next steps Your next due-diligence checks: Review Mangopay wallet custody and platform flows Compare Ryft's marketplace payout and holding model Review Lemonway's marketplace safeguarding model Shortlisted Mangopay, Ryft, or Lemonway? Model their real all-in cost — processing, FX, payouts, and hidden fees — against your monthly GTV and cross-border share. Open the payment cost calculator Path C4 Path C4: Seller payouts, holding required, outside Europe Shortlist Airwallex — describes platform payment use cases for marketplaces; coverage varies by region. 7 Checkout.com — integrated platform capabilities covering onboarding, accepting payments, transferring funds, and paying users. 8 Rapyd — a third candidate: broad local-method acceptance and payout corridors. For all three, the real decision is whether the model is available for your entity, your countries, and your release rules. Nuvei — worth evaluating as a payment and multi-currency settlement layer if your holding need can be met through a wallet or delayed-settlement arrangement rather than legal escrow; its local acquiring coverage in Latin America and Europe is strong, 18 but it is not an escrow substitute. PayU — can serve as the acceptance and split-settlement layer in its core corridors (Eastern Europe, LatAm, India, Africa — see the corridor note in Path C2 ), 23 but pair it with a separate custody answer; it is not the holding layer. Local champions — dLocal or EBANX (Latin America), Xendit (Southeast Asia), Razorpay (India), Flutterwave (Africa) can cover local acceptance and payouts, but few offer a holding arrangement; verify custody separately before shortlisting. Skip / Watch-outs Do not treat any of these names as proof of escrow: a platform payments product is not automatically a legally recognized escrow service. Do not begin with a regional wallet provider before mapping your recipient countries. "Outside Europe" still includes very different licensing, onboarding, and payout requirements. If your release conditions require a legally recognized custody arrangement, keep the escrow-focused candidates as the primary shortlist. Write down the exact release event. Delivery? Service completion? A dispute window? Another condition? Ask the provider to explain the legal custody model. Ask what happens if the condition is challenged. Confirm the answer in the agreement. Do not rely on a sales demonstration. Next steps Your next due-diligence checks: Check Airwallex marketplace coverage and payout design Review Checkout.com's integrated platform payment flow Shortlisted Airwallex, Checkout.com, or Rapyd? Model their real all-in cost — processing, FX, payouts, and hidden fees — against your monthly GTV and cross-border share. Open the payment cost calculator Path C5 Path C5: Partner revenue share, simple rules Shortlist PayPal — dependable payout tools. A fixed share paid to a predictable group of partners needs dependable recipient onboarding and payout operations, not a full marketplace build. 2 Airwallex — documents connected accounts and fund splitting. 3 Country and feature availability need checking for both the sender and the recipients. Tipalti — built for exactly this job: mass partner payouts with recipient onboarding and tax-form collection across a wide country list. If the recipients are contractors rather than revenue-share partners, Deel's API bundles payouts with contractor compliance — a different product category, but sometimes the right one. (If you need affiliate tracking bundled with payouts rather than just payment rails, dedicated partner platforms like Impact 25 or PartnerStack 26 sit a layer above payment processors.) Skip / Watch-outs Skip Finix. A heavier platform implementation is hard to justify for simple commission rules. Skip an escrow-oriented design. Commissions paid on a schedule do not automatically need conditional custody. Refunds are the blind spot. A partner may already have received commission. Then the underlying customer payment is refunded or disputed. Decide now. Claw back the commission? Net it against future payouts? Absorb the loss? Then confirm the provider's reporting model can support that policy. Also confirm the recipient is actually a partner. If they are selling through your platform, your operational and compliance responsibilities are different. Next steps Your next due-diligence checks: Check PayPal's partner payout country and recipient limits Review Airwallex connected-account and split-payment integration Check Tipalti's mass payout coverage and onboarding flow Shortlisted PayPal, Airwallex, or Tipalti? Model their real all-in cost — processing, FX, payouts, and hidden fees — against your monthly GTV and cross-border share. Open the payment cost calculator Path C6 Path C6: Partner revenue share, complex rules Shortlist Adyen — documents platform onboarding and configurable split instructions. 10 Still requires a fit check for your business and markets. Braintree (PayPal Enterprise Payments) — belongs on this shortlist if your platform already sits in the PayPal ecosystem and needs multi-tier splitting with conditional releases; its Marketplace product handles sub-merchant onboarding and split logic that PayPal Commerce's standard payouts cannot. 20 Finix — documents platform payment flows supporting seller onboarding and payments. 9 (Note: Finix serves US- and Canada-based platforms with US-style domestic underwriting — verify non-US founder eligibility before shortlisting. 29 ) Worldpay for Platforms — now part of the Global Payments / Worldpay combined entity (GPN completed the acquisition in January 2026); 19 the enterprise-grade option in the same category, aimed at larger software platforms. For platforms above roughly $10M+ annual processing volume, the Integrated & Platforms channel is worth a separate enterprise inquiry, but expect a heavier underwriting process than Finix or Adyen. Tiered shares. Caps. Multiple recipients. Conditional releases. These rules must cover allocation, fees, reversals, and reporting — this is a scoped technical and underwriting conversation. Skip / Watch-outs Do not start with PayPal alone. A basic payout product may leave your application calculating and reconciling complex entitlements. Do not become a payment facilitator just because your rules are complex. A partner solution may cover the operations without the full PayFac model — Adyen describes a service model that lets platforms embed payments without becoming a fully licensed payment facilitator. 11 US-centric trap: a US LLC alone does not qualify you. A wave of newer PayFac-as-a-service providers — Tilled, Forward, Rainforest, Stax Connect — and US payout rails such as WePay and Dwolla underwrite only platforms that have a US-resident principal: an owner or guarantor who lives in the United States and holds an SSN. A non-US founder's US LLC with an EIN does not meet that requirement — the application is typically rejected at the underwriting stage, before any integration work pays off. Before building a plan around any provider in this category, get its principal and residency requirements in writing. Next steps A spreadsheet of rules is not an implementation plan. Define who earns each share. Define which event makes it payable. Define caps and exceptions. Define how refunds alter the ledger. Define who approves overrides. Ask each provider to demonstrate with four scenarios. A real transaction. A refund. A partial reversal. Month-end reconciliation. Do this before you commit. Your next due-diligence checks: Review Finix platform onboarding and payout integration Review Adyen for Platforms split and reconciliation flows Review Braintree Marketplace sub-merchant onboarding and split logic Shortlisted Adyen, Braintree, or Finix? Model their real all-in cost — processing, FX, payouts, and hidden fees — against your monthly GTV and cross-border share. Open the payment cost calculator Result You only collect payments for yourself You do not need a Stripe Connect replacement just because your business is outside the United States. Connect is built for platform flows involving other recipients. Customers pay your business. You do not split proceeds. Start with a regular payment-provider comparison instead. Go to the Stripe Alternatives Hub Looking for a way to avoid being the seller of record at all? If you sell digital products or SaaS, see the Merchant of Record Hub . The model rarely covers physical goods or offline services. Before you commit Before you commit: can you afford the migration? A move away from Connect is not a rate switch. Engineering has to change API endpoints, card credential portability, webhooks, reconciliation, and historical records. If you cannot assign at least one full-time backend engineer for four to six weeks, the migration may cost more than the marginal improvement you expect. See the full platform payment gateway switch cost comparison Before you sign Before you sign Do not negotiate on headline rate alone. Minimum volume, rate tiers, termination, rolling reserve, and mid-term price changes are where platform contracts hide cost. See the five contract questions and negotiation checklist Reverse filter Reverse filter: When should you stay on Connect? Stay if your split rules are simple. Stay if recipients are concentrated in one country. Stay if you do not need to hold funds. Stay if the migration is more expensive than the likely improvement. Stay if your team cannot spare the engineering time. Changing providers creates operational risk as well as code work. In those cases, ask a smaller question first. Can adding another payout route or improving reconciliation solve the pain without replacing the whole payment system? If your entity is in the US or UK, Stripe's own Global Payouts is exactly that kind of smaller question: it sends payouts to recipients in 160+ markets without a Connect build. Platforms incorporated elsewhere cannot use it yet — verify eligibility before counting on it. Consider leaving if you need a genuine escrow arrangement your current structure does not provide. Consider leaving if cross-continent payouts have become a material cost or delivery bottleneck. Consider leaving if your split rules require code that repeatedly fights the Connect model. Stripe's manual payout feature is not escrow. A business needing escrow must verify a different legal arrangement. It cannot simply extend a payout delay. 6 Two edge cases deserve restraint. If volume is falling but migration is even more expensive, stay for now. Assess whether a payout layer can solve the specific problem. If volume is rising but your team has no integration capacity, consider a Merchant of Record model for eligible products. If you are already on Stripe and your product is purely digital, Stripe Managed Payments is the lowest-switching-cost MoR option — but it explicitly excludes Connect, Express accounts, and platform-managed accounts, so it only applies if you are willing to drop the multi-seller architecture entirely. 21 Or add a payout layer before replacing the entire stack. An MoR is not a universal substitute for marketplace settlement. Confirm who becomes the seller. Confirm which obligations the agreement actually transfers. 14 The purpose of this guide is not to push you away from Connect. It is to show where to go when leaving solves a real problem — and why staying can be the better decision when it does not. If no traditional provider will serve your region at all, this guide won't solve it. See Stablecoin & Crypto Payout Rails instead. Next steps Follow the right child page If your real question is company formation or tax structure, start with the Corporate Formation Hub and Merchant of Record Hub . If you are unsure whether you need a Connect-like platform function or an MoR, clarify the Merchant of Record definition first. Then compare vendors. If your concern is non-US founders, account access, or identity requirements, read the Stripe Alternatives Hub . Also read the EIN and SSN explainers. And if a US PayFac-as-a-service name catches your eye, read the US-centric trap warning first — most of them require a US-resident principal. If your immediate worry is an account freeze or losing access to payouts, use the Account Freeze Playbook if that page is available. Do not use a company-formation article to answer a seller-payout question. Do not use an MoR article to answer an escrow question. Route by the part of the money flow that is actually breaking. Then compare the provider pages for that path. FAQ FAQ Can I use Stripe Connect without a US LLC? Possibly. Availability depends on the platform's country, the recipients' countries, and the payment flow. Check Stripe's current supported-country rules before forming a US company by default. 15 What is the difference between split payments and escrow? Split payments decide who receives which share of a transaction. Escrow is a legal custody arrangement with conditions for releasing funds. Delaying a payout does not, by itself, make the arrangement escrow. 16 17 How much does it cost to migrate from Stripe Connect? There is no reliable flat price. Engineering time, card credential portability, reconciliation changes, and parallel testing drive the work. Migration cost is modeled separately from day-to-day processing cost — see the Marketplace Payment Migration Cost Comparison for engineering hours, token portability, and timeline trade-offs. For ongoing processing, FX, and payout fees, use the payment cost calculator . Can I use PayPal for payouts in India? PayPal's current payout documentation lists India for receiving and withdrawing. That does not guarantee that every sending business, currency, or platform route is eligible. One concrete limit: PayPal's payout support for India covers receiving and withdrawing, but currency conversion is excluded — in practice, incoming payouts are converted to INR at PayPal's rate before reaching the recipient's bank. Factor that conversion cost into your payout economics, and check sender-country approval and recipient requirements before building around the route. 2 When should I become a PayFac myself? Only after you have compared the operational, regulatory, and commercial burden with a provider or PayFac-as-a-Service model. A complex partner split alone is not a reason to take on that responsibility. 11 What is the difference between PayPal Commerce, Braintree, and PayPal Enterprise Payments? PayPal Commerce is the standard collection and payout product. Braintree is PayPal's full-stack acquiring and platform-splitting product, integrated into PayPal's Payment Services & Crypto division after the April 2026 reorganization and positioned under the PayPal Enterprise Payments name. For simple mass payouts, PayPal Commerce is sufficient; for marketplace-grade splitting with sub-merchant onboarding, Braintree is the relevant product. 20 Why don't you list Square, Shopify Balance, or Mollie? Different jobs. Square processes payments in only eight countries and is built around a single merchant of record, not multi-party seller payouts. 27 Shopify Balance is a financial account for US Shopify merchants to receive their own Shopify payouts faster — it is not a rail for paying your platform's sellers. 28 Mollie is a legitimate European split-payments option — see the note in Path C3 — and it drops out of the shortlists only where the flow needs heavier regulated custody or coverage beyond Europe. 24 Appendix Appendix: Why route by who receives the money? Most "alternatives" lists make the decision harder. A list organized by annual sales assumes your size is the main variable. It is not. A feature-by-feature comparison gives you a menu. It leaves you to work out which features matter. A single-platform review tells you what a provider offers. It does not answer your real question: which model fits the way my business moves money? Start with the recipient. A seller payout is one job. A partner commission is another. A payment collected only for your own business is a third. Then narrow by whether money must be held before release, then by geography. Finally, check two things: does the operational benefit justify migration, and does the contract protect you as the business changes? A split payment alone does not establish escrow, and it does not determine who is legally selling to the customer — those depend on the actual flow, the agreement, and applicable rules. 16 17 Sources https://docs.dodopayments.com/features/mor-introduction https://developer.paypal.com/payouts/supported-features https://www.airwallex.com/docs/payments-for-platforms/overview https://www.airwallex.com/docs/banking-as-a-service/market-and-infrastructure-coverage https://docs.mangopay.com/guides/e-wallet-system https://docs.stripe.com/connect/manual-payouts https://www.airwallex.com/docs/payments-for-platforms/use-cases/payments-for-marketplaces https://www.checkout.com/products/integrated-platforms http://docs.finix.com/guides/platform-payments https://docs.adyen.com/platforms/online-payments/split-transactions https://www.adyen.com/knowledge-hub/payfac-as-a-service https://docs.stripe.com/connect/migrate-to-stripe https://docs.stripe.com/connect/webhooks /glossary/mor/ https://docs.stripe.com/connect/cross-border-payouts-to-recipients /glossary/split-payments/ /glossary/escrow/ https://www.nuvei.com/posts/alternative-payment-methods-what-they-are-why-they-matter-and-how-to-choose-them-for-your-business https://investors.globalpaymentsinc.com/news-releases https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/marketplace/overview https://docs.stripe.com/managed-payments https://www.nuvei.com/posts/nuvei-to-acquire-payoneer-for-2-75-billion-creating-a-leading-global-platform-for-local-and-cross-border-commerce https://docs.payu.in/docs/split-settlements https://www.mollie.com/products/connect https://impact.com/ https://partnerstack.com/ https://developer.squareup.com/docs/international-development https://www.shopify.com/balance https://www.finix.com/

title: Paddle vs Stripe 2025: 5% Fee & Hidden Costs Audit
description: Paddle's 5% fee vs Stripe's 2.9%: Our 2025 audit reveals Paddle saves $7,049/year by handling global tax compliance. See the full cost breakdown.
text:
🔍 Transparency Note: This review is based on an independent audit of Paddle’s 2025 fee structure. While we may earn a commission if you sign up through our links, no payment processor paid for this content or influenced our LumScore™. Audit Context: Calculations assume a SaaS company with $50k MRR, 250 transactions/mo, and customers in the US, EU, and UK. See Calculation Methodology Paddle vs Stripe 2025: 5% Fee & Hidden Costs Audit Written by Alex Shi Published on December 18, 2025 Paddle charges 5% per transaction while Stripe charges 2.9%. Yet for a $50,000/month SaaS business selling globally, Paddle saves you $7,049 annually compared to Stripe’s complete tax compliance stack [8] . 
        The reason? Stripe Tax only calculates tax amounts—you still register for VAT/GST/sales tax IDs in each jurisdiction, 
        file monthly returns, and remit payments manually [21] [25] . This December 2025 audit breaks down the total cost of ownership for both platforms, reveals when Paddle’s Merchant of Record model justifies the premium, and exposes the API limitations your engineering team will hate (but your CFO will forgive). Before we dive into the granular cost breakdown, here is the executive summary of our audit findings: Paddle LumScore™ 88 The Verdict: "The only viable payment stack for founders who fear tax audits more than API limits." 👍 Best For Global SaaS ($20k-$500k MRR) scaling to EU/UK. 🚫 Avoid If US-only sales or Enterprise ($1M+ MRR) needing custom revenue recognition. ✓ The Good Saves $7,049/yr vs Stripe + Compliance Stack (at $50k MRR). Zero Liability: Paddle assumes legal responsibility for tax audits (MoR). Global Reach: Instantly compliant in 100+ jurisdictions (VAT/GST). AI Recovery: Includes ‘Paddle Retain’ to recover ~10% of failed payments. No Admin: Eliminates 15-20 hours/month of finance reconciliation work. ✕ The Bad API Rate Limits: Hard cap at 240 requests/minute (vs Stripe’s 6,000). Rigid UI: Cannot fully customize checkout CSS (PCI requirement). Cost: 5% fee is expensive if you only sell domestically (US-only). Payouts: Minimum payout threshold exists; transfers aren’t instant like Stripe. The $38,549 Problem: What Stripe’s 2.9% Doesn’t Include Stripe Tax is not a Merchant of Record—it’s a tax calculation engine charging an additional 0.5% fee [21] . For a $50k MRR SaaS with customers across the EU, UK, Australia, and multiple U.S. states, your actual monthly cost with Stripe looks like this: Monthly cost breakdown: Stripe’s $3,232 unbundled stack versus Paddle’s $2,625 all-inclusive fee. [Download Chart] Stripe Payment Processing: $1,450 (2.9% of $50k) [23] Stripe Tax (Calculation Only): $250 (0.5% of $50k) [25] TaxJar Professional: $199/month for automated sales tax calculations [29] Tax Filing Services: $450/month (10 jurisdictions at $45 per filing) [21] CPA Reconciliation: $500/month for quarterly compliance review and nexus monitoring Economic Nexus Tracking: $100/month (manual monitoring or Anrok add-on) [27] Annual Tax Registrations: $83/month amortized ($1,000/year for 10 jurisdictions) [21] Risk Buffer: $200/month (late filing penalties, audit prep) Total Stripe Stack: $3,232/month ($38,549/year) Compare this to Paddle’s all-inclusive $2,625/month ($31,500/year for 5% + $0.50 per transaction) [1] . The 5% fee includes payment processing, global tax registration in 100+ jurisdictions, monthly/quarterly filing, remittance to tax authorities, and legal liability for tax errors [4] . 📝 How We Calculated These Numbers (Methodology) To ensure this audit is fair and transparent, we modeled a specific mid-market SaaS scenario rather than using generic averages: Scenario: B2B SaaS company with $50k MRR and $200 Average Order Value (250 transactions/month). Geography Breakdown: 40% US (Nexus triggered in 5 states), 30% EU, 10% UK, 20% Rest of World (no tax). Stripe Stack Assumptions: Includes “TaxJar Professional” ($199/mo) required for automated reporting, plus a conservative CPA retainer ($500/mo) for quarterly nexus checks and filing oversight. Paddle Stack Assumptions: Standard pricing of 5% + $0.50 per transaction. No custom enterprise discounts applied. The Merchant of Record Advantage: Who Goes to Tax Jail? As a Merchant of Record, Paddle becomes the legal seller of your products [8] . This distinction fundamentally shifts tax compliance responsibility: What Paddle Does (That Stripe Doesn’t) Tax Compliance Task Paddle (MoR) Stripe Tax VAT/GST/Sales Tax Calculation ✅ Included ✅ Included (0.5% fee) [25] Tax ID Registration (100+ jurisdictions) ✅ Paddle registers ❌ You register manually [21] Monthly/Quarterly Tax Filing ✅ Paddle files ❌ You file via TaxJar/CPA [29] Tax Remittance to Governments ✅ Paddle pays ❌ You pay manually Economic Nexus Monitoring ✅ Automatic tracking ❌ Manual monitoring required [27] Audit Liability ✅ Paddle assumes legal risk ❌ Your company audited EU VAT MOSS Registration ✅ Single registration for 27 countries ❌ You register in each country Paddle handles tax registration, filing, and remittance in over 100 jurisdictions [4] . When tax authorities audit transactions, they audit Paddle’s books, not yours . One SaaS founder on Reddit summarized it: “Stripe Tax calculates VAT but doesn’t file it. I still need TaxJar ($199/mo) + an accountant ($500/mo). Paddle does all of this for the 5%.” [9] The FTC Settlement: Legitimacy Concerns Addressed In 2025, Paddle paid a $5 million FTC settlement for facilitating tech-support scam payments through its MoR infrastructure [web:2] [web:5] . Paddle disputes processing those specific transactions, stating the fine relates to third-party abuse of the platform. For legitimate SaaS businesses, Paddle’s MoR model remains operationally valid—they process over $4 billion annually [web:8] . However, this incident highlights the importance of vetting any Merchant of Record partner, as they legally represent your brand in customer transactions. The Developer Reality Check: What Your Engineering Team Will Complain About 📢 Note to the Engineering Team: Paddle’s API has constraints that will frustrate developers accustomed to Stripe’s flexibility: Rate Limits: 240 requests/minute maximum [2] [11] —compared to Stripe’s 6,000/minute. Exceeding this triggers 429 errors and temporary blocks [12] [13] . Checkout Customization: You cannot fully customize checkout UI/CSS like Stripe [3] [web:3] . Paddle controls the branded checkout flow to maintain PCI compliance as the MoR. Discount Management: “Quite limited” according to December 2025 G2 reviews—no native bulk code generation [3] . Integration Ecosystem: Fewer third-party connectors than Stripe, though Churnkey and Framer support exists [16] . 🛡️ For the Founder: Does This Matter? No. You trade 10% UI flexibility for 100% tax compliance automation. The 240/min rate limit handles up to 345,600 API calls daily—sufficient for SaaS businesses under $5M ARR. The checkout customization constraint is the price of having Paddle : Register for VAT MOSS across 27 EU countries [4] Monitor economic nexus thresholds in 50 U.S. states File 120+ tax returns annually on your behalf This saves you 15-20 hours per month that your finance team would spend reconciling TaxJar → Stripe → QuickBooks → government portals. At a $50/hour valuation, that’s 240 hours annually worth $12,000—on top of the $7,049 cash savings. What Verified Users Say (December 2025 G2 Reviews) G2 reviews from December 2025 highlight consistent strengths [3] : “Support team is responsive and helpful” “Handles taxes, compliance, subscription management smoothly, so I can focus on developing products” “Reliable checkout system and international coverage help increase conversions” The platform ships quarterly major updates [6] . November 2025 releases included a dashboard redesign and expansion to 60+ local payment methods (KakaoPay, NaverPay for Korean markets). Paddle Retain uses AI to predict churn risk based on payment failure patterns and automate dunning workflows [5] , though this is a premium add-on beyond the base 5% fee. The Break-Even Analysis: When Does Paddle Stop Making Sense? Paddle remains cheaper until approximately $85,000 MRR for multi-jurisdiction sellers. [Download Chart] Paddle’s 5% fee becomes more expensive than Stripe’s unbundled stack at approximately $85,000 MRR —assuming you need multi-jurisdiction tax compliance. Below that threshold, the fixed costs of TaxJar ($199), filing services ($450), and CPA reconciliation ($500) make Stripe’s total cost higher despite the lower percentage fee. Choose Paddle If You Check 3+ of These: ✅ You sell to customers in 5+ countries (EU VAT, UK, Australia, Canada, multi-state U.S.) ✅ Your MRR is between $20k-$500k (the cost-efficiency sweet spot) ✅ You don’t employ a dedicated tax compliance manager ✅ You value liability protection over API flexibility ✅ Your finance team’s time is better spent on forecasting than TaxJar reconciliation ✅ You’ve triggered economic nexus in multiple U.S. states but haven’t registered yet Choose Stripe If You Check 3+ of These: ✅ You operate in 1-2 U.S. states only (minimal tax complexity) [21] ✅ Your MRR is under $15k (5% fee too expensive) or over $1M (negotiate custom Stripe rates) [23] ✅ You need extreme checkout customization or white-label payment flows ✅ You already employ a full-time tax accountant ($75k/year salary) [27] ✅ Your product requires 6,000+ API calls/minute [11] ✅ You prefer unbundled services where you control each component ⚖️ A Counter-Perspective: Why a CPA Might Prefer Stripe “If a company plans to go public (IPO), we often prefer Stripe. It keeps the financial data ‘raw’ and in-house, giving us granular control over revenue recognition policies (ASC 606). Paddle’s MoR model simplifies things by ‘black-boxing’ the revenue, which can be annoying for enterprise-grade audits later on.” lumscope.com’s Take: Valid point. If you are prepping for an IPO, use Stripe. If you are trying to survive to $1M ARR, use Paddle. The Verdict: Is 5% Still Worth It in December 2025? Buy Paddle if: You’re a founder who values sleep-at-night compliance over developer flexibility, operates in multiple tax jurisdictions, and would rather invest 240 hours annually into product development than tax reconciliation. The $7,049 cash savings plus eliminated audit risk justifies the 2.1% premium over Stripe’s base rate [1] [23] . Avoid Paddle if: You operate in a single low-complexity market, your engineering team requires deep payment flow customization, or you’ve already built tax infrastructure with in-house expertise. The 5% fee becomes pure overhead once you surpass $85k MRR without international expansion. The question isn’t whether 5% is expensive. It’s whether $7,049 annually + 240 hours of reclaimed time + zero tax audit liability is worth 2.1% more in fees. For SaaS founders expanding globally between $20k-$500k MRR, the math favors Paddle—even if your CTO disagrees. A Merchant of Record (MoR) is a legal entity that takes full responsibility for payment processing, tax collection, and compliance on behalf of your business. For SaaS companies and digital product sellers, this means offloading one of the most complex operational burdens: global sales tax. Why SaaS Founders Need Independent MoR Solutions When you sell software or digital products internationally, you’re legally required to collect and remit sales tax (VAT, GST, etc.) in dozens of jurisdictions. Each country has different rules, thresholds, and filing requirements. A MoR handles all of this for you. ❌ Without MoR (DIY) Register for tax in 30+ countries Track changing tax rates manually File quarterly/monthly returns Handle audits and disputes Maintain compliance documentation ✅ With MoR (Automated) MoR is the seller of record Automatic tax calculation MoR files all tax returns MoR handles audits 100% liability transfer Key MoR Platforms 🏢 Paddle The market leader for B2B SaaS. Platform risk refers to the vulnerability of relying on a single payment provider. When your account gets frozen or terminated—often without warning—your entire revenue stream stops instantly. Why Mainstream Processors Flag Legitimate Businesses Payment processors use automated risk models that often misclassify compliant businesses as “high-risk.” Common triggers include: Dropshipping & E-commerce: High chargeback rates, even if legitimate Digital Products: Intangible goods trigger fraud alerts Consulting & Coaching: Advance payments for future services Travel & Events: Long time gaps between payment and delivery Subscription Models: Recurring billing patterns flagged as suspicious The Backup Account Strategy Smart businesses don’t wait for disaster. text: lumscope.com Methodology (Payment Infrastructure Focus) The lumscope.com Methodology Two Frameworks, One Mission We don’t just “compare” payment providers. We audit their infrastructure resilience. At lumscope.com, we reject surface-level “Top 10” lists. We believe that choosing payment infrastructure should be as rigorous as choosing your banking partner. That’s why we developed a dual framework : the Resilience Audit measures platform risk, while the True Cost Model calculates total operational expenses. Together, they answer both “Can I trust this provider?” and “What will it really cost me?” Framework 1: The Resilience Audit Platform Risk Assessment A standardized evaluation system that assesses payment provider reliability across four critical dimensions. Every provider must prove its resilience in our Evidence Protocol to earn trust. 1. 🛡️ Platform Risk Score (25%) The Freeze Test Can you survive an account freeze? We Check: Account freeze frequency, appeal process quality, and business model tolerance (high-risk, dropshipping, digital products). We Reject: Providers with opaque risk models that freeze accounts without warning. 2. 🔄 Backup Feasibility (25%) The Redundancy Test Can you maintain a backup account? We Check: Multi-account policies, load balancing capabilities, and failover setup complexity. We Reject: Providers that prohibit backup accounts or make redundancy technically impossible. 3. 💰 Cost Transparency (25%) The Hidden Fee Test What are you really paying? We Check: Pricing documentation clarity, hidden fees (per-account, chargeback, currency conversion), and volume threshold transparency. We Reject: Providers with opaque “contact sales” pricing or undisclosed fee structures. 4. 🌍 Geographic Coverage (25%) The Scale Test Can you scale globally? We Check: Multi-region processing, local payment method support, and currency conversion capabilities. We Reject: Providers limited to single-region operations or with poor international support. Framework 2: The True Cost Model Total Cost of Ownership Analysis Most payment comparisons stop at advertised rates. We calculate the hidden operational expenses that turn “cheaper” providers into budget traps. The Iceberg Principle A provider advertised at 2.9% + $0.30 isn’t cheap if you must pay $2/account for split payments, hire a tax consultant ($6,000/year), and spend 240 hours annually on manual compliance. We quantify these “shadow costs” and add them to the advertised rate to reveal the true Total Cost of Ownership (TCO). 💼 Per-Transaction Fees Beyond the advertised rate: per-account charges, chargeback fees, refund fees, currency conversion markups, and cross-border transaction surcharges. 🔧 Integration Overhead What third-party tools must you purchase to make the provider functional? (Tax automation, fraud prevention, subscription management add-ons.) ⚖️ Compliance Burden If the provider doesn’t handle tax/compliance, who pays for it? Quantifying liability transfer and manual labor is part of TCO. How the Two Frameworks Work Together Resilience Audit (High Risk) tells you: “Stripe has a history of freezing accounts for high-risk business models without warning.” True Cost Analysis tells you: “For your $100k/month marketplace, Stripe Connect costs $4,800/year more than Adyen for Platforms due to per-account fees.” Together, they answer: “Is this provider both reliable AND cost-effective for my business?” The Evidence Protocol In every guide, you will see our Evidence Protocol . This is where we cite the specific source for every claim we make—official pricing documentation, API capabilities, user migration experiences, and verified compliance requirements. We do the research so you can make the decision.

title: EIN Number for Non-US Founders: Format, Application & Lookup
description: What is an EIN? Learn how non-US founders can apply for a US Employer Identification Number without an SSN, the 9-digit format, lookup steps, and EIN vs ITIN.
text: EIN (Employer Identification Number): How Non-US Founders Get a US Tax ID (No SSN) Getting paid from outside the United States can mean navigating business paperwork before you can open an account. The good news is that many non-US founders can apply for an EIN without an SSN. This guide explains the exact process, what documents to prepare, and where delays usually happen. What is an EIN Number? (Definition & Full Form) EIN is short for Employer Identification Number . It is a nine-digit number, usually written as 12-3456789 , that the IRS assigns to a business entity for federal tax filing and reporting. Put simply, think of it as a Social Security Number for your company : it identifies the business, not its founder. An EIN can appear on tax forms, payroll records, bank applications, and payment-provider onboarding. It belongs to the entity, not the owner, and does not create a company by itself. A bank or payment processor may ask for it along with formation documents and identity checks. EIN vs. SSN vs. ITIN: Business vs. Individual Tax IDs An SSN identifies an individual. An ITIN is an individual tax-processing number for someone who needs a U.S. taxpayer ID but is not eligible for an SSN. A TIN (Taxpayer Identification Number) is the broad umbrella term; an EIN is the business type of TIN. In short: ITIN is for a person, EIN is for an entity. If a form asks for a "federal tax ID number," it usually means the company’s EIN. If you live outside the U.S. and are not eligible for an SSN, you do not need to borrow someone else’s number. IRS Form SS-4 instructions say to enter “Foreign” or “N/A” on line 7b when the responsible party does not have and is ineligible to obtain an SSN or ITIN. Note for international founders: Local tax IDs are completely different. UK founders may need a UTR for UK tax matters; it is not a U.S. EIN. In India, the MSME EIN used in Odisha is a separate Indian registration term, not the U.S. Employer Identification Number. Banks and payment companies may request an EIN during KYB (Know Your Business) checks. Mercury (a popular US bank for non-residents), Stripe, and Airwallex commonly ask for business and ownership documents. An EIN can help with onboarding, but it does not guarantee approval. Without suitable business documents, you may be stuck with high-fee alternatives like PayPal. How to Apply for an EIN Without an SSN (Form SS-4) The standard application is Form SS-4 . First, confirm your entity’s legal name and structure. If a provider requires a U.S. LLC or corporation, form it before applying; an EIN alone does not form a company. Get the current SS-4 and instructions from IRS.gov. The online application is limited to eligible applicants with a U.S. or territory location and qualifying taxpayer ID, so many international founders use phone, fax, or mail. Enter the entity’s legal name and mailing address as shown on its formation documents. Use an address where you can receive IRS mail and keep it consistent with other applications. Complete lines 7a–7b. Put the responsible party’s legal name on 7a. If that person has no SSN or ITIN and is ineligible to get one, enter “Foreign” or “N/A” on 7b. Do not substitute a passport number in that field. Answer the business questions accurately. Complete the LLC and entity-type sections, choose the real reason for applying, provide the relevant start date, and say whether the entity has received an EIN before. Keep your foreign passport handy to confirm your name and for separate bank identity checks. Sign, date, and submit once. Keep a copy of the form and proof of transmission. The IRS advises using one application method per entity to avoid duplicate EINs. [SYS_NOTICE]: FAXING FROM OUTSIDE THE U.S. IRS International Fax Line: +1 (304) 707-9471 IRS U.S. Fax (No U.S. Location): +1 (855) 215-1627 Recommended Stack: Use digital fax utilities (e.g., FaxZero, eFax) to submit Form SS-4. Ensure your return fax number is configured to receive the IRS confirmation page 4–7 business days later. If you have no legal residence or office in the U.S., the IRS lists an international telephone application option. For planning, allow four to eight weeks in case your application needs follow-up. Mailed applications can take about four weeks. EIN Lookup and Verification: How to Check Your Number Save your CP 575 EIN assignment notice and a copy of Form SS-4. There is no universal public EIN lookup tool for most private companies, so the IRS notice is usually the best proof. If you applied online and were eligible to use the tool, you can view and save the assignment notice at the end of the process. If you lose the notice, contact the IRS to ask about an EIN verification letter, commonly called Letter 147C . Be ready to prove you are authorized to receive the information. Banks and payment processors may request the CP 575, 147C, or a matching tax document, so make sure your legal name and EIN match across all records. DIY vs. Agency: Cost and Processing Time Route / Provider Cost Timeline & Compliance Infrastructure Action Pure IRS DIY $0 (Free) 4–7 business days via Fax; up to 4 weeks via Mail. You must source your own Registered Agent address. Read Manual Doola ~$297 Includes U.S. LLC formation, state filing, Registered Agent, and managed EIN processing. Launch Platform ↗ Firstbase ~$297 Streamlined non-resident onboarding + immediate access to Mercury/Wise banking networks. Launch Platform ↗ DIY makes sense if your U.S. entity already exists and you are comfortable following the IRS instructions. However, if you are starting from scratch and need a U.S. LLC, you will need a Registered Agent —a service with a physical U.S. address required by law to receive legal and tax documents on your behalf while you live abroad. Paid agencies bundle this seamlessly. ⚠️ The KYB Warning for Multi-Vendor Platforms While obtaining an EIN allows you to open a standard corporate bank account at Mercury or Wise, it does not bypass the structural compliance walls of Stripe Connect if your core operating business model is a multi-vendor marketplace. If you are setting up a platform with split-payout architectures and want to avoid the complex U.S. corporate tax liabilities that come with an EIN-backed LLC, read our comprehensive 2026/2027 Stripe Connect Alternatives (No LLC) Report . Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) Does an EIN expire? An EIN generally does not expire or get reassigned to another business. If your ownership or structure changes, or the business closes, check IRS guidance to see whether you need to notify the IRS or apply for a new number. Can non-US residents get an EIN without a US LLC? Sometimes. An EIN does not prove you formed a U.S. LLC, and a non-U.S. resident may need one for a foreign business or another IRS-recognized tax purpose. If a bank requires a U.S. entity for business banking, an EIN alone is not enough. Is an EIN the same as a Tax ID? An EIN is one type of federal Tax ID (TIN) for a business. "Tax ID" can also mean an SSN or ITIN for a person, or a state or foreign tax number. Check which type a form asks for before entering a number.

title: SSN (Social Security Number): Non-US Founder Payment Guide
description: No SSN? Non-US founders can still get paid. Learn how payment gateways verify you via EIN and passport, plus the one U.S. representative exception.
text: SSN (Social Security Number): What Non-US Founders Need to Know for Payment Gateways An SSN (Social Security Number) is a nine-digit identification number issued by the U.S. Social Security Administration (SSA) to track individuals for tax and social security purposes. If you are a non-US founder, you do not need an SSN to get paid. Payment gateways care about your business identity , not your personal US work authorization. Here is the one-line distinction you need before reading further: EIN = Company tax ID (what you need for business accounts). ITIN = Individual tax ID (for personal US tax filing). SSN = US person's work ID (you do not have this). TIN = The umbrella term for all of the above. Why You Don't Have an SSN — and Why It Doesn't Block Payments The SSA generally issues SSNs to noncitizens only when they are authorized to work inside the United States. As a founder living and operating a business outside the US, you are simply not in that category. A missing founder SSN is not a universal bar to getting paid. Instead of an SSN, your business is identified by its own tax ID (like an EIN), while your personal identity is verified using your passport. What Payment Gateways Actually Ask For (and What They Don't) When you open a merchant account, a payment provider typically asks for: Company details: Legal name, entity type, registration country, and business activity. Tax identification: An EIN for a US company, or a local business tax ID. Formation documents: State-filed records or equivalent local registration documents. Owner information: Legal names, addresses, ownership percentages, and passport copies. The US Representative Rule: A form labeled "SSN" may be asking about a specific person, not the company. Stripe's published rules, for example, distinguish US representatives from non-US representatives. If you register a US account and designate a US-resident representative, that representative must provide the last four digits of an SSN or ITIN. A non-US representative, however, can provide a local tax ID and passport. Never assume an EIN belongs in an SSN field. Read exactly which person the field is asking about. The 4 Real Scenarios for a Non-US Founder Stop reading generic guides. Find your exact scenario in this matrix to see what you actually need: Founder Scenario Entity Location SSN Required? Required Tax ID / Proof Viable Payment Stack A. Local Digital Seller Home Country (Non-US) No Local Tax ID + Passport Local PSP, Paddle, Lemon Squeezy B. US LLC Owner US ( Wyoming / Delaware) No (Unless US Rep) EIN + Foreign Passport Mercury, Airwallex, Stripe C. Foreign Entity + US Gateway Home Country (Non-US) No Local Docs + W-8BEN-E Airwallex (Global), Mangopay (EU) D. US Tax Filing Anywhere No (Use ITIN) ITIN (Form W-7) Tax compliance only (Not for onboarding) Note on Sole Proprietorships: if you apply to Stripe as an individual US sole proprietor rather than through a US LLC, you cannot use a company EIN. In that specific case, an SSN or ITIN is required for the individual applicant. Strategic Notes on Scenarios Scenario A (Local): You don't need a US LLC just because you have US customers. Use a Merchant of Record (MoR) like Paddle to handle US sales tax and avoid US entity requirements. Scenario B (US LLC): If you plan to form a US LLC, you will need to apply for an EIN. You can use services designed for non-US founders, such as Doola or Firstbase , which handle remote registration and EIN filing without an SSN. For banking, Mercury accepts non-US founders with a US entity and passport. Scenario C (Foreign Entity): If you want to use a US-based gateway but keep your local entity, check their supported countries. If they require a US entity for your product, that is an entity-eligibility issue, not an SSN issue. Common Traps When You Read "SSN Required" Avoid these 4 fatal errors during onboarding: Confusing Entity ID with Personal ID. Do not put an EIN into a field asking for an SSN. Ask support: "Is this field for the business representative or the company?" Incomplete KYB Stack. Passports prove personal identity; EINs prove business existence. You need the full stack. A passport alone won't pass a KYB check. Fabricating or Borrowing an SSN. Never make up a number or use someone else's. It is an immediate, permanent KYB rejection trigger and constitutes identity fraud. Ignoring Structural Eligibility. A perfect tax ID won't fix an unsupported country, a prohibited high-risk industry, or missing US operations proof. This includes using a VoIP number (e.g., Google Voice) or a virtual mailbox flagged as a Registered Agent address instead of verifiable business operations. 📋 Copy-Paste Support Verification Script When contacting Stripe, Mercury, or Airwallex support, do not rely on their general FAQ. Copy and paste this exact script to get a definitive answer: I am a non-U.S. resident founder. The business is registered in [Your Country]. The application form requires an SSN. 1. Is this SSN field for the business representative or the company? 2. Can I submit my foreign passport and local tax ID instead? 3. Does this specific account type require a U.S.-resident representative, or can I use my non-U.S. status? ⚠️ The "No-LLC" Escape Hatch If you do not want to form a US LLC, obtain an EIN, or deal with US representative rules, you have another path. You can use an MoR (Merchant of Record) or a platform that supports local entities globally. If you want to avoid the US corporate structure entirely, read our comprehensive 7 Stripe Connect Alternatives (No LLC) Report to see which platforms accept non-US entities and handle the compliance for you. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) Can I use Stripe without an SSN? Possibly. If you have a US account, Stripe allows a non-US representative to use a local tax ID and passport. However, if you designate a US-resident representative, they must provide an SSN or ITIN. Does Mercury require an SSN? No. Mercury accepts international founders. You need a US-registered company, an IRS-issued EIN document, and a passport for identity verification. What if I use a fake SSN? Do not. Payment providers run real-time checks against the SSA and credit bureaus. A fake SSN will trigger an immediate rejection and may permanently ban your business entity from the platform.

title: TIN (Taxpayer ID) for Non-US Founders: What to Enter
description: Stuck on a payment form's TIN field? TIN is a label, not a new number. See whether to enter your EIN, local tax ID, or VAT/GST to avoid KYB stalls.
text: TIN (Taxpayer Identification Number): What Non-US Founders Should Enter on Payment Forms You reach an onboarding form and see a box labeled "TIN." Should you enter your EIN, a local tax number, or something else? Start with this: TIN is an umbrella term. It is not a number you apply for. It is a label for a number you already have. The right number depends on whose information the form requests, which country it covers, and whether it names a specific ID such as an EIN. TIN Is an Umbrella Term — That's Why the Form Uses It TIN stands for Taxpayer Identification Number . In U.S. tax documents, it is a category that includes an SSN , an EIN , an ITIN , and other IRS-issued numbers. An EIN identifies a business; an ITIN identifies an individual for certain federal tax purposes. Payment platforms sometimes use "TIN" more broadly. They may mean the tax identifier issued by your country, not a U.S. number. That could be a company tax ID, a VAT or GST number, or another official identifier. Read the full field label, not just the word "TIN": "EIN" or "U.S. TIN" points to a U.S.-issued number. For a U.S. company, that is usually its EIN. "Foreign TIN" or "Local tax ID" points to the tax identifier issued in the relevant non-U.S. jurisdiction. "VAT" or "GST number" asks for that specific registration number, not a generic company number. "Business registration number" may mean a company registry ID, which can differ from the company's tax ID. Four Real TIN Scenarios for a Non-US Founder Find your situation, then type the number in the last column. Scenario Applicant What the form usually asks for Type this in the field A. U.S. LLC Your U.S. company Company EIN, or "U.S. business TIN" Your company's EIN, format XX-XXXXXXX B. Local company outside the U.S. Your non-U.S. company Foreign TIN, local tax ID, or VAT/GST Your local company tax ID, or the specific VAT/GST number requested C. U.S.-source income as an individual You, personally Foreign TIN on Form W-8BEN The foreign TIN requested, or the form's stated alternative if you are not legally required to have one D. No U.S. entity, gateway accepts non-U.S. entities Your local entity or you as sole proprietor Local tax ID for the applicant The local tax ID for the business or person named as the applicant Two rules that apply to all four scenarios: Do not put a personal ITIN in a company EIN field. The EIN belongs to the business; the ITIN belongs to an individual. A mismatch between the company name and the tax ID is a common reason a KYB check stalls. Do not treat the company registration number as the tax ID. Some countries issue them separately. If the form asks for a VAT number, enter the VAT number, not the company registry number. How to Find Your TIN / EIN in Practice For a U.S. company's EIN , check the IRS confirmation notice, commonly known as CP 575. If you have misplaced it, use official IRS channels. Eligible users can download an EIN verification notice from a Business Tax Account; the current notice can substitute for older CP 575 notices and Letter 147C. Some providers also accept CP 575 or Letter 147C as proof of an EIN. Do not rely on a third-party site that claims it can look up any private company's EIN. EIN documents must match the exact legal entity named in the application. For a local company tax ID , check the tax registration certificate, VAT or GST registration, business license, or official tax authority account. Use the identifier the form requests, not whichever number is easiest to find. Match the number to the legal name on the tax record. Providers compare names and tax IDs against government information. A mismatch can trigger a request for more documents or delay verification. Follow the form's formatting rules — some add hyphens automatically, others expect digits only. Common TIN Mistakes That Trigger KYB Rejection Putting the wrong identifier in the wrong field. The most common version: a personal ITIN in a company EIN field, or a local tax ID in a field that explicitly says "U.S. TIN." "TIN" alone can be broad, but "U.S. TIN" is specific. Treating Form W-9 as a generic international TIN form. W-9 is for U.S. persons. Foreign individuals or entities generally need a W-8BEN or W-8BEN-E . The correct form depends on who receives the income and the entity's tax classification, not nationality alone. Using different identifiers for the same company without understanding why. One provider may ask for the company's EIN, another for its local tax ID. That can be valid if each form requests a different identifier. Keep a record of which number belongs to which entity and field. Leaving a required field blank or inventing a number. A blank required field stops the application before review. A fabricated number creates a name–tax-ID mismatch. Both are KYB rejection triggers. Never use another person's SSN, ITIN, EIN, or local tax ID. 📋 Copy-Paste Support Verification Script When a TIN field is ambiguous, do not guess. Send this to the provider's support: I am a non-U.S. resident. The applicant is a [company registered in X / individual]. The form asks for a "TIN." 1. Does this field mean a U.S. TIN (EIN) or my local company tax ID? 2. Which specific number should this entity enter? 3. If I do not have the requested number, what alternative document do you accept for this account type? ⚠️ If You Have No U.S. Entity at All If you do not want to form a U.S. LLC, obtain an EIN, or deal with U.S. TIN fields, you still have a path. A Merchant of Record (MoR) or a gateway that supports local entities can handle compliance on your behalf. See our 7 Stripe Connect Alternatives (No LLC) Report for platforms that accept non-U.S. entities. If you do decide to form a U.S. company, Doola and Firstbase handle remote registration and EIN filing without an SSN. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) Is my TIN the same as my EIN? No. An EIN is one type of U.S. TIN used to identify a business. A form may use "TIN" for another identifier, including an individual or foreign tax ID. What is my TIN if I don't have an SSN? If the applicant is your U.S. company, its EIN may be the requested number. If the applicant is a non-U.S. company, the form may ask for its local tax ID. Check the exact wording. What if I don't have a U.S. tax ID at all? If the form accepts a foreign or local TIN, enter the identifier issued to the applicant by its jurisdiction. If it specifically requires a U.S. TIN, ask the provider whether your account type accepts another document or number. Do not invent a number or substitute an unrelated ID.

title: ITIN vs EIN for Non-US Founders: Payments vs Tax Guide
description: ITIN vs EIN for non-US founders: EIN unlocks Stripe & Mercury accounts; ITIN is only for US personal tax filing. See when to skip Form W-7 and use your passport.
text: ITIN (Individual Taxpayer Identification Number): When Non-US Founders Actually Need It You have an EIN . Now a payment form mentions an ITIN. Do you need both? For most non-US founders, the answer is no . An EIN unlocks payment accounts; an ITIN is strictly for U.S. personal tax filing. Here is the core distinction before you apply for anything: EIN : Company tax ID (what Stripe, Mercury, and Airwallex ask for). ITIN: Individual tax-processing number (only for personal U.S. tax returns). SSN : U.S. work authorization ID (non-residents are not eligible). TIN : The umbrella label for all of the above. What an ITIN Actually Is (and What It Is Not) An ITIN is a nine-digit number issued by the IRS to individuals who need a U.S. taxpayer ID for federal tax purposes but are not eligible for an SSN. What it is NOT: An ITIN is not a company tax ID. It does not identify your LLC, prove business registration, or serve as a banking credential. Getting an ITIN before forming a company will not speed up payment gateway approval. ITIN vs. EIN vs. SSN: The Payment Decision Matrix For a U.S. business account, providers verify two separate subjects: the company (via EIN and formation docs) and the human representative (via passport and local tax ID). Tax ID Subject Primary Purpose How Payment Gateways Use It EIN Company U.S. business tax & banking ID Required to verify U.S. LLCs/Corps on Mercury , Airwallex, and Stripe. ITIN Individual Personal U.S. federal tax filing Not required for business onboarding unless you are a U.S.-resident representative. SSN Individual U.S. citizen/resident tax & work ID Required only if you designate a U.S.-resident account representative. The Stripe Representative Exception: Stripe's U.S. rules distinguish U.S.-resident representatives (who must provide the last four digits of an SSN or ITIN) from non-U.S. representatives (who provide a foreign passport and local tax ID). Unless you appoint a U.S. resident to manage your account, you do not need an ITIN for Stripe. When a Non-US Founder Actually Needs an ITIN You do not need an ITIN simply because you own a U.S. LLC, hold an EIN, or open a U.S. business bank account. You only need to apply for an ITIN (via IRS Form W-7 ) if you meet one of these specific conditions: Personal U.S. Tax Filing: You have U.S.-sourced personal income that requires filing a U.S. federal income tax return (Form 1040-NR). Tax Treaty Benefits: You are claiming specific U.S. tax treaty exemptions as an individual. Counterparty Requirement: A specific U.S. payer or financial institution explicitly requires an ITIN under a written contractual rule. The W-7 Filing Path: DIY vs. Certified Acceptance Agent (CAA) If you do need an ITIN, the standard application uses Form W-7 . The IRS generally requires a federal tax return to be attached unless an exception applies. A passport is one accepted identity document—and this is where applicants face a real decision. DIY path: You mail your original passport to the IRS along with Form W-7. The IRS returns it after processing, but the passport is in transit and in IRS custody for weeks. The IRS itself says to allow 7 weeks for a status notice, or 9 to 11 weeks during tax season or when applying from overseas. If your passport is lost or delayed, you cannot travel internationally until it is resolved. CAA path: An IRS-authorized Certifying Acceptance Agent (CAA) can authenticate your passport copy without you mailing the original. You send the copy to the CAA, the CAA verifies it against the original in a video call or in person, and the CAA submits the W-7 package to the IRS. Your passport never leaves your hands. Cost comparison: CAA fees typically run $100–$300 per application, depending on the agent and whether dependents are included. The DIY path costs $0 in fees but carries the risk of original-document loss and the time cost of international mail. For a founder whose passport is the only travel document, the CAA fee is often the cheaper option once you price in the risk of being without a passport for 7–11 weeks. Do not choose a CAA just because it is faster—it is not necessarily faster. Choose it because it removes the original-document risk. If you have a second valid passport or a national ID accepted by the IRS for your country, DIY may be fine. Actionable Next Steps by Setup If you are forming a U.S. LLC: Skip the ITIN. Focus on getting your company formation docs and EIN. Services like Doola or Firstbase handle non-resident LLC setup and EIN filing without an SSN or ITIN, allowing you to onboard onto Mercury using just your passport. If you want to avoid U.S. tax paperwork entirely: You don't need a U.S. LLC, an EIN, or an ITIN just to sell globally. Use a Merchant of Record (MoR) or read our 7 Stripe Connect Alternatives (No LLC) Report to find gateways that accept your local home-country entity. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) Can I open a U.S. bank account with just an ITIN? No. An ITIN is a personal tax number, not a business registration. To open a U.S. business account at Mercury or Airwallex, you need a registered U.S. entity, an EIN, and your foreign passport. Do I need an ITIN if I own a single-member U.S. LLC? Not automatically for payment onboarding. While single-member LLCs have specific IRS information-reporting rules (such as Form 5472 and pro-forma Form 1120), those are entity-level filings that use your EIN , not a personal ITIN. Consult a cross-border CPA for your specific tax filing obligations. What if a payment form asks for "SSN or ITIN"? If you are applying on behalf of a U.S. company as a non-U.S. resident, check whether the field refers to the human representative. Most gateways allow non-U.S. representatives to bypass the SSN/ITIN box by selecting non-U.S. citizenship and uploading a foreign passport. Do I need a CAA to apply for an ITIN? No. You can file Form W-7 directly with the IRS by mailing your original passport. A CAA is optional and is used to avoid mailing the original document. The trade-off is a fee of roughly $100–$300 versus the risk of being without your passport for 7–11 weeks.

For Stripe, the surcharge depends on your entity: 1% for US entities and 2% for non-US entities. For Airwallex, we apply the standard platform rate and a 0.5% major-currency FX markup. PayPal FX spread modeled at 3% (conservative lower bound of PayPal's 3–4% range). Airwallex rates depend on the entity you sign up with. Select your entity in the calculator. When you change the entity selector at the top of the page, the Airwallex entity follows the closest match until you override it manually inside the Airwallex card — your manual choice is remembered on your next visit. A note on Europe: EEA card pricing varies by card type (consumer vs. commercial). This version uses flat reference rates per platform; card-type splits are planned for a future version. All rates come from public sources: Stripe public pricing, Airwallex entity pricing pages, and PayPal's public FX spread. Rates shown are standard public defaults for comparison, not custom quotes. High-volume platforms can usually negotiate lower rates with all three providers, so treat the output as a baseline for comparison rather than a quote. Rates last checked: November 2026. Before you sign: marketplace payment gateway contract checklist The calculator tells you what a provider costs per month. It does not tell you what it costs to leave, or what breaks when you do. Before signing, confirm each item below. Exit terms Early termination fee: what does it cost to leave before the contract ends? Auto-renewal: does the contract renew automatically, and what is the notice window? Bundled services: if you unbundle, which services stop working? Data portability Token export: can you export tokenized card data, or will you re-collect payment details? Historical transactions: what format and time window are available on exit? API documentation: do you retain access after termination? Pricing traps Minimum monthly fee: what is the floor, and does it reset monthly? Tiered pricing: what triggers the next tier, and is it retroactive? Mid-term price changes: what notice period applies? Migration cost Engineering hours: how many backend weeks to re-integrate? Reconciliation rework: how much of your finance reporting depends on the current provider? Parallel running: do you need to run both systems during a transition window? FAQ How is this different from a seller fee calculator? This page models platform-side costs: the processing and FX fees your marketplace pays on the volume it moves through each provider. A seller fee calculator estimates what each seller pays on their own sales — it does not show what the platform itself spends per month. Why don't you include Finix, Dwolla, or WePay? These providers require a US-resident principal with an SSN for underwriting. Non-US founders typically cannot pass their risk checks, so they are not realistic options for the audience of this guide. What does "conservative FX estimate" mean? PayPal's FX spread actually ranges from 3% to 4% depending on the currency pair. The calculator uses 3% as the lower bound so the comparison does not overstate PayPal's cost.
